chapters.name: Which line mattered?
chapters.note: a word? a paragraph? a sentence?

cap.1: A reasoning model writes pages of working before it answers. To ask which bit mattered, you first have to decide what a 'bit' is.
cap.2: Reasoning models spread their computation across thousands of tokens, so single-token tools from circuit work don't reach it. A word is too small to mean anything; the whole trace is too big to poke.
cap.3: Computation is serialised across many tokens, so token-level analyses like IOI don't transfer. Thought Anchors (Bogdan, Macar, Nanda, Conmy, 2025) makes the sentence the unit of analysis.

cap.1: Picture a long hike. Most steps are just walking. At one fork you say 'let's take the ridge path', and that single choice decides where you end up.
cap.2: Most sentences in a trace are routine steps. A thought anchor is the rare one, often a plan or a 'wait, let me reconsider', that sets the course everything after it follows.
cap.3: A thought anchor is a sentence with outsized causal influence on the rest of the trace and the final answer. Found three ways: resampling, counterfactual replacement, and attention analysis via receiver heads.

cap.1: Replay the hike from that spot many times, sometimes keeping the sentence, sometimes rewriting it. If the endings change a lot, it was an anchor.
cap.2: Resampling importance: regenerate the trace from sentence i many times with it kept, and many times with it re-rolled, then compare the two final-answer distributions. A big gap marks an anchor.
cap.3: Importance is a distance between answer distributions conditioned on keeping versus resampling sentence i. Counterfactual importance asks instead what happens if the sentence had been different.

cap.1: Draw each sentence as a dot and each strong influence as an arrow. Most dots nudge only their neighbour. The anchors reach all the way to the answer.
cap.2: Illustrative graph. In the course's replication of the paper's Figure 3b, plan and uncertainty-management sentences carry positive mean counterfactual importance: planning and backtracking steer.
cap.3: Sentence-to-sentence influence forms a causal graph over the trace. Grouped by label, plan_generation and uncertainty_management show positive mean counterfactual importance (the Figure 3b replication).

right.title: careful pipeline
lines: decimals and list markers kept whole

chapters.verdict: Every score is indexed by chunk: the cut and the labels are part of the measurement.

cap.1: Before you can score sentences you have to cut the text into them. Cut carelessly and scores land on the wrong sentences, with nothing to warn you.
cap.2: Importance scores are indexed by chunk position, so a splitter that breaks '3.14' shifts everything after it. And in a first-match keyword labeller, the order of the word lists decides the label.
cap.3: Segmentation instability propagates straight into the causal graph. CATEGORY_WORDS is scanned in insertion order, so generic words placed early swallow sentences and flatten per-category importance.

props.label: maths traces: set up, plan, fact, compute, doubt, pull together, check, answer
safety traces: situation assessment, leverage identification, self-preservation

cap.1: Today's unit is the sentence, sorted into eight jobs for maths. Safety traces get different labels. The labels are a lens you choose, not a law.
cap.2: Current method: circuit tools work token by token and don't reach long reasoning. Emerging research (Thought Anchors, 2025): use sentences, with labels chosen per domain. What you need: labels that fit your question.
cap.3: The eight-way taxonomy is the paper's Section 3; [4.3] section 4 swaps in situation_assessment, leverage_identification, self_preservation. Unit and taxonomy are modelling choices: check scores are stable under them.

chapters.name: Why it matters
items: Find where the decision really happened
Plans and doubts are where to look
Then intervene on that one sentence

cap.1: In pages of reasoning, a few sentences do the steering. Find them and you know where the model really decided, which is where understanding and steering start.
cap.2: Anchors tell you which steps to read closely, which to resample, and where an intervention would change the outcome. The same tools carry over to safety traces and agentic runs.
cap.3: Sentence-level causal attribution localises decisions in long chains of thought: the groundwork for auditing reasoning, testing faithfulness, and targeted interventions to understand and steer models.

caption.1: Slide how hard this sentence commits to answer A, then how often a re-roll just says the same thing again. Watch the kept and re-rolled bars pull apart, or not.
caption.2: Resampling compares answers with the sentence kept versus re-rolled. Re-rolls that repeat the same idea dilute the gap, which is why counterfactual importance looks only at re-rolls that differ.
caption.3: In this toy, with total-variation distance, resampling importance = (1 − b) × counterfactual importance: re-rolls that restate the sentence (share b) are wasted samples.

where_else: Receiver heads: the white-box route to the same anchors, through attention
Safety traces: the same method with a situation-assessment, leverage and self-preservation taxonomy
Long agentic runs: which step of a tool-using trace actually decided the outcome
Games and projects: an opening move or early design decision that fixes everything after it

hamming.what: A sentence in a reasoning trace whose presence disproportionately shapes the rest of the trace and the final answer.
hamming.when: When you need to know which steps of a long chain of thought actually decided the answer, for example before reading closely or intervening.
hamming.why: Most sentences are routine; finding the few that steer shows where the model's decision really happened, and where to look or intervene.

object.title: The stepping-stone trail
object.subtitle: A reasoning trace as stepping stones, one per sentence: most lead only to the next, two fan out all the way to the answer.

cap.1: A reasoning trace as stepping stones, one per sentence. Most stones just lead to the next.
cap.2: Nodes are sentence chunks in order; edges are strong influences of one sentence on a later one.
cap.3: A sentence-level causal graph: nodes are chunks, edges mark large counterfactual effects of an earlier chunk on a later one.

cap.1: Two stones have extra paths: a plan and a moment of doubt. Their influence reaches all the way to the answer.
cap.2: The plan sentence and the 'wait, check that' sentence are the anchors: many downstream sentences depend on them.
cap.3: Anchors show high out-degree in the influence graph; plan_generation and uncertainty_management carry positive mean counterfactual importance in the Figure 3b replication.

cap.1: From above: ordinary stones touch only their neighbours, anchors fan out to everything after them.
cap.2: Out-degree is the tell. A routine computation step changes little if you re-roll it; an anchor changes the rest of the trail.
cap.3: Resampling an ordinary chunk leaves the answer distribution roughly unchanged; resampling an anchor shifts it, which is what the importance score measures.

cap.1: The answer sits downstream of both anchors. Their arrows are what resampling measures.
cap.2: The white-box route looks for the same stones through attention: later sentences keep attending back to the anchors.
cap.3: Black-box resampling and white-box attention analysis (receiver heads) are complementary routes to the same anchors, and [4.3] works through both.

predict.why: Plans and backtracking set the course; in the Figure 3b replication those categories carry positive mean counterfactual importance.

predict.q: Re-rolled many times, a sentence mostly comes back saying the same thing. Its resampling importance will be...

options.t: Understated: most samples never tried an alternative

predict.why: Re-rolls that restate the sentence dilute the gap. Counterfactual importance keeps only the re-rolls that differ.

predict.q: Your splitter breaks '3.14' into two chunks. What happens to later importance scores?

options.t: They shift onto the wrong sentences

predict.why: Every importance score is indexed by chunk position, so segmentation errors propagate straight into the causal graph.

object.where: Anywhere one early decision fans out: an opening move, an early design choice, a plan sentence in a chain of thought.
